title: Unique identifier linking in user data store
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account data containing unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that can link data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in user data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes (email, username, etc.) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data to individuals through attribute combination.

title: Processing of identified parent account data
description: The system requests and processes identified parent account data, which directly identifies the data subject.

title: Unique identifier in user account data
description: The MongoDB users collection contains unique references to the identity of the data subject through user account identifiers.

title: Quasi-identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification.

title: Attributable data evidence from stored accounts
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their account or actions.

title: Potentially sensitive parent account data types
description: Parent account data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required by the authentication service functionality.

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Parent account data may be stored in the MongoDB collection longer than functionally needed for the authentication service.

title: Excessive party access to parent account data
description: Parent account data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators or other services.

title: Unawareness of parent account data storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their parent account data is being collected, stored, or processed by the authentication service.

title: Lack of user control over data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their parent account data is processed, stored, or retained.

title: Lack of control for data rectification and erasure
description: Users may lack the ability to rectify incorrect parent account data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed and stored than is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Parent account data may be stored in the MongoDB collection longer than functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for the stored parent account data.

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: The JWT token transmitted in this flow contains a unique identifier that can directly identify the data subject to the parent user.
assumptions: JWT tokens typically contain user identity claims that are unique to the authenticated user.

title: User data contains quasi-identifiers
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., email, role, department) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify the data subject.
assumptions: User data typically includes multiple attributes that, when combined, can uniquely identify an individual.

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: The unique identifier in the JWT can be used to link this data flow to other data flows or systems, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the user across the system.
assumptions: JWT tokens are designed to be unique and persistent identifiers that can be correlated across different contexts.

title: Potentially sensitive user data transmitted
description: User data transmitted in this flow may include sensitive personal information that exceeds what is functionally required for the authentication service to communicate with the parent user.
assumptions: User data may contain sensitive attributes beyond what is needed for basic parent-child relationship management.
uncertainty_note: Depends on what specific user data is included in the transmission.

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: User data is shared with the parent user (EE1), which is a predetermined external party. This creates exposure of personal data to an external entity.
assumptions: The parent user is an external entity that receives personal data from the authentication service.

title: User unaware of data transmission to parent
description: The data subject may not be aware that their user data and JWT are being transmitted to the parent user in this flow.
assumptions: Users may not have visibility into all data flows originating from authentication services.
uncertainty_note: Depends on user consent mechanisms and transparency in the system.

title: Limited user control over data sharing with parent
description: Users may lack control over how their data is shared with the parent user, including preferences for what data is transmitted and when.
assumptions: The authentication service may not provide granular consent controls for data sharing with parent users.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the system's consent and preference management capabilities.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The transmission of user data alongside JWT may process more personal data than is functionally required for the authentication service to communicate with the parent user.
assumptions: Data minimization requires that only data strictly necessary for the purpose is processed and transmitted.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the user data transmitted is actually necessary for the parent-child relationship functionality.

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Email addresses are globally unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of parent email and password creates a quasi-identifier that can uniquely identify the parent-child relationship and potentially link to other data.
assumptions: Email+password combination is unique to the parent-child pairing

title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) to authenticate the child user.
assumptions: Email and password are personally identifiable information

title: Identifier processing
description: Parent email is a unique identifier that directly references the parent's identity, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Email addresses are unique identifiers

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly necessary for authentication functionality.
assumptions: Passwords are sensitive authentication credentials

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Password data may be stored, logged, or processed beyond what is functionally needed for authentication, creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Passwords should not be retained after authentication

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: Child user may not be aware that their login transmits parent's email and password, and the implications of this data processing.
assumptions: Children may lack understanding of privacy implications

title: Lack of consent preferences
description: Child user has limited control over how parent's personal data is collected and processed during authentication.
assumptions: Children cannot meaningfully consent to parent data processing

title: Data minimization violation
description: Collecting parent email and password for child authentication may process more personal data than functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Child's consent may not be valid for processing parent's personal data, as children typically lack legal capacity to consent to such data processing.
assumptions: Children cannot provide valid legal consent

title: Linking through JWT identifier
description: The JWT token contains unique identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of the child user across different authentication contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens contain unique user identifiers that persist across sessions

title: Linking through child profile quasi-identifiers
description: Child profiles may contain combinations of attributes (age, location, interests) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data across different sources when combined with other information.
assumptions: Child profiles contain multiple attributes that can be combined to identify individuals

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The authentication service processes identified child data through JWT tokens and child profiles, which contain personal information that directly identifies the child user.
assumptions: JWT and child profiles contain identifiable personal data about children

title: Processing of unique identifiers in JWT
description: The JWT token contains unique references to the identity of the child data subject, enabling direct identification of the individual.
assumptions: JWT tokens contain unique user identifiers that reference the child's identity

title: Excessive data type sensitivity for child profiles
description: Child profiles may contain more sensitive personal data than functionally required for authentication purposes, including potentially sensitive information about the child.
assumptions: Child profiles contain data beyond what is needed for authentication

title: Excessive volume of child data processed
description: The authentication service processes an excessive amount of child personal data beyond what is functionally needed for the authentication process.
assumptions: Full child profiles are transmitted when only authentication credentials are needed

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: Children as data subjects may not be aware that their personal data is being collected, processed, and transmitted through the authentication service.
assumptions: Children lack the capacity to fully understand data processing implications

title: Lack of child control over data preferences
description: Children lack the ability to set preferences or provide meaningful consent regarding how their personal data is processed and stored.
assumptions: Children cannot meaningfully consent to data processing

title: GDPR violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing child data may violate GDPR data minimization principles if more personal data is collected and processed than is actually needed for the authentication functionality.
assumptions: GDPR applies to child data processing and requires data minimization

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Processing of child personal data may not rely on valid consent, as children cannot provide legally valid consent and parental consent mechanisms may be insufficient.
assumptions: Children cannot provide valid consent under GDPR

title: Linking through unique user identifiers
description: Child User actions (video search, request, like, comment) are linked to the user through unique identifiers (user ID, account ID) that persist across all interactions with the Video Management Service.
assumptions: The system maintains persistent user identification across all video-related activities.

title: Profiling individual through video behavior patterns
description: Video search queries, likes, and comments can be analyzed to create behavioral profiles of the Child User, revealing preferences, interests, and potentially sensitive information about the user.
assumptions: The Video Management Service collects and stores metadata about user interactions for analytics purposes.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The Video Management Service processes identified data including user video content, search queries, and interaction data that are directly linked to specific users.
assumptions: Video content and user interactions are stored with user identification.

title: Revealing attributes through video content
description: Video content, search queries, and comments may contain revealing attributes (location, interests, activities) that support identification of the data subject beyond just the user ID.
assumptions: Video content and comments may contain personally identifiable information or context that reveals user attributes.

title: Attributable video interaction data
description: Video search, request, like, and comment actions can be attributed to specific users, preventing denial of these actions.
assumptions: All user interactions are logged and associated with user accounts.

title: Detection through observed video communications
description: Video search queries, requests, likes, and comments can be observed and detected by the system, potentially revealing user interests and activities.
assumptions: The system logs and monitors all user interactions with video content.

title: Collection of sensitive video data beyond functional needs
description: Video content and detailed interaction data may be collected that is more sensitive than functionally required for basic video search and management functionality.
assumptions: The system collects video metadata and content that may be more sensitive than necessary for the stated functionality.

title: Unnecessary analysis and enrichment of video data
description: Video data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed (e.g., for recommendations, analytics) beyond what is necessary for the core video search and management functionality.
assumptions: The Video Management Service performs additional processing on video data for purposes beyond basic functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video interaction data may be shared with predetermined third parties (e.g., analytics providers, advertisers) beyond what is functionally necessary for the video management service.
assumptions: The system shares user interaction data with external parties for analytics or advertising purposes.

title: Unawareness of video data processing
description: Child Users may not be fully aware of the extent of video data collection, processing, and storage that occurs when they search, request, like, or comment on videos.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data processing activities.

title: Lack of control over video data processing preferences
description: Users may lack adequate control to set preferences regarding how their video search, like, and comment data is processed, stored, and shared.
assumptions: Privacy settings may be limited or difficult to configure for video-related data processing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The Video Management Service may process more personal data (video content, detailed interaction metadata) than is actually needed for the stated functionality of video search and management.
assumptions: Data collection and processing exceeds what is necessary for the core functionality.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video content is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved video to a child.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video data may be streamed at a finer granularity than necessary, potentially revealing more personal details than required for the child viewing.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is needed for simple streaming functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is shared with a static set of parties (the child user) which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The system processes video data that is identified with the child user, potentially revealing personal information.

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content may contain revealing attributes (location, activities, environment) that support identification of the data subject.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in video
description: Video content may contain multiple quasi-identifiers (time, location, activities) that can be combined to link data to an individual.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video data can be analyzed for patterns to link data to the individual child user, potentially revealing behavioral patterns.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child user may not be fully aware that their video data is being collected, processed, and streamed.

title: Lack of preference control
description: The child user may lack control over preferences regarding how their video data is processed or what data is collected.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data processing may exceed what is actually needed, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Potential invalid consent
description: Video data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from the child or guardian.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, IP addresses) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple attributes (page views, timestamps, device info) that can be combined to create quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification of individuals.

title: Profiling an individual through browsing patterns
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data to build profiles of individuals, linking their interests, behaviors, and preferences to specific users.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (e.g., user IDs, session tokens) that are processed and shared with advertisers.

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data includes revealing attributes such as visited pages, search queries, and time spent on content that can support identification of data subjects.

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Personal data is propagated to external services (advertisers) where it may not be functionally needed for the core recommendation engine functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is made accessible to a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, expanding exposure beyond what may be necessary.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected, processed, and shared with third-party advertisers.

title: Lack of control over data sharing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their browsing data is shared with advertisers.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (browsing data) is processed and shared than is actually needed for the functional goals of the recommendation engine.

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Personal data collection and sharing with advertisers may not rely on valid consent from data subjects.

title: Processing of identified data - Government ID images
description: The Authentication Service processes government ID images which are clearly identified personal data that directly identifies individuals.

title: Identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (government ID numbers, biometric data) that directly reference the identity of the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in ID images
description: Government ID images reveal multiple identifying attributes including facial features, name, ID number, and other personal information that supports identification of the data subject.

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Storing them in a file system may exceed functional necessity.

title: Data retention duration concerns
description: Unclear how long government ID images are retained in the file system. Storage may exceed functionally needed duration, violating storage limitation principles.

title: Excessive party access to ID images
description: File system storage may grant access to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services that may not need access to government ID images.

title: Unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in the file system, as this is a backend storage operation not directly visible to users.

title: Lack of user preferences control
description: Data subjects likely have no control over how their government ID images are processed, stored, or retained in the file system.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to request deletion or rectification of their government ID images stored in the file system.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: Storing government ID images may violate the data minimization principle if the images are more personal data than actually needed for authentication purposes.

title: GDPR storage limitation violation
description: Unclear retention policies for government ID images may violate GDPR storage limitation principle requiring data to be kept no longer than necessary.

title: Potential invalid consent for ID image storage
description: Unclear whether data subjects provide valid, informed consent for storing their government ID images in the file system, which may be required under GDPR.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable or quasi-identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of attributes in child history (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child when combined.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes child history which is identified personal data belonging to the child (data subject).
assumptions: Child history contains personal data that identifies the child
